Commentary.Commentary: 205 to win then. Can Bermuda offer a fight? Stay tuned...

George Munsey has a chat with Dirk Nannes. Says that he struggled at the start, aiming to go square square, which he reflects now, was a poor option. But is happy to have learnt that quickly. Feels that the pitch is a beautiful one to bat and could get better under lights. Backs his bowlers to stick to their plans and execute them.
Bermuda started well with the ball but once they got under the pump, they could not react well. Leverock picked up 2 wickets but was expensive while the others were not that impressive.

It did not start off that well for Scotland, as they lost two wickets pretty cheaply. But then, the Munsey-MacLeod stand changed the tempo. Their 76-run stand in 39 balls injected some much-needed momentum and after Munsey departed, MacLeod took off. He started pummeling the bowling to all parts and eventually finished with 74 at a strike rate of 200.
Wow. 204. Massive, massive, massive total. 'They will win by 104 runs', chides my colleague. Jokes apart, this will give a massive boost to Scotland's net run rate.

OUT! Calum MacLeod departs after playing a fantastic innings. On a length on middle, MacLeod looks to play a scoop shot but does not get the timing on it. It goes towards square leg where George O'Brien takes the simplest of catches. It has been an excellent innings from MacLeod. SCOTLAND END WITH 204/4 IN THEIR 20 OVERS.

The players are out in the middle. George Munsey and Kyle Coetzer will open for Scotland. George O'Brien to start off proceedings to Munsey. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Robert Key observing the track and finds Bermuda grass. Detailing, says that there is green live grass along with some patchy, bare grass. Means, he adds that this pitch will be two-paced.

Scotland captain, Kyle Coetzer, says that it is not a bad pitch to bat on and would like to take that opportunity tonight. Admits that the campaign for them has not gone well but they are confident of getting things on track. Informs that Josh Davey has been left out for Alasdair Evans.

Rodney Trott, Bermuda skipper, says that the reason to field is because the pitch has something in it, so he wants to take a chance. Says that he is confident of his team's batsmen doing well on this pitch which should get better as the game progresses.

Bermuda (Playing XI) - Dion Stovell (IN FOR Janeiro Tucker), Oronde Bascome (IN FOR Deunte Darrell), Allan Douglas (IN FOR Malachi Jones), Delray Rawlins, Onais Bascome, Kamau Leverock, Okera Bascome, Terryn Fray, Rodney Trott(c), George O'Brien (IN FOR Derrick Brangman) and Sinclair Smith(wk).

Scotland (Playing XI) - Kyle Coetzer(C, IN FOR CRAIG WALLACE), George Munsey, Calum MacLeod, Oliver Hairs (IN FOR MICHAEL LEASK), Richie Berrington, Matthew Cross(wk), Tom Sole, Mark Watt, Safyaan Sharif, Alasdair Evans (IN FOR JOSH DAVEY) and Hamza Tahir.
TOSS - We are hearing that Bermuda have won the toss and inserted Scotland in. Probably the decision is due to the dew factor. We shall see later.

We are all set for the final match of the day! Bermuda take on Scotland in match number 30, under lights, in Dubai. With 4 losses on the trot, Bermuda are almost out of the competition, barring any miracle. Scotland, though, have not done any favours to themselves with inconsistent performances so far. A clinical display tonight will be the need of the hour.
